can_do_statement: Can use 'could' with a limited range of verbs to make suggestions.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses 'could' + limited verbs (e.g., go, have, take) as a gentle directive or suggestion.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency: offering a choice to the listener

positives: We could have dinner after that, if you want.
You could go to Versailles.
negatives: She could speak French when she was younger.
Could you pass the salt?

can_do_statement: Can use 'could I' to seek permission.

ontology.mental_model: Agent shifts focus to themselves with 'could I' to ask for authorization or permission.

positives: Could I take the class that I will miss on Saturday?
Could I play with it now, please?
negatives: I could run very fast when I was a kid.
We could meet later.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could' to talk about possibility.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses 'could' with abstract subjects (it, this) to assess likelihood or potential truth.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance: stepping back to evaluate probability

positives: it could be really fun to have a talkative person
Could this really happen?
negatives: Could you pass the salt?
We could have dinner after that.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could' with an increasing range of verbs to make suggestions.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses 'could' to propose varied actions as possibilities for the listener.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency: offering a broader array of choices

positives: We could meet in the nice cafe next to your house.
you could become a member of a gym.
negatives: I could jump really high back then.
Could I get a glass of water?

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses 'could have' + past participle to conceptualize a past possibility that did not occur or is uncertain.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance: looking back at an alternative past

positives: In fact it could have been dangerous.
What could have happened?
negatives: I could have a dog if I wanted.
We could have dinner after that.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could have' + '-ed' form to express disapproval or criticism.

ontology.mental_model: Agent directs disapproval toward another entity (usually 'you' or 'they') for failing to perform a desired past action.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency: asserting normative expectation on another's past behavior

positives: I think that you could have arranged entertainment.
you could have given them a better service
negatives: I could have done that if I had time.
It could have been worse.

can_do_statement: Can used affirmative 'could' have + '-ed' to talk about past possibility.

ontology.mental_model: Agent reflects on alternative outcomes or missed opportunities using abstract or passive subjects.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance: distancing from the actual past to explore a counterfactual

positives: her mother could have phoned her but she did not.
all these problems could have been avoided
negatives: I couldn't have bought it.
You could have asked me.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could have' + '-ed' to talk about regrets.

ontology.mental_model: Agent looks inward at their own past actions, expressing a counterfactual wish using 'I/we'.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance: stepping back to evaluate one's own missed chances

positives: I wish I could have stayed, especially to help the children.
I could have listened more to my team members.
negatives: You could have given them better service.
It could have been dangerous.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could have' + '-ed' to speculate about the past.

ontology.mental_model: Agent posits theories about uncertain past events, typically involving third parties or hypotheticals (who, a thief, she).
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance: distancing to deduce possible past realities

positives: I thought perhaps a thief could have entered my house.
who could have saved her?
negatives: I wish I could have stayed.
You could have given me more time.

can_do_statement: Can use 'could' as the past form of 'can' in reported speech.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses 'could' within a subordinate clause to backshift 'can' to the past after a reporting verb.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance: temporal distance via reported speech backshifting

positives: I told them I couldn't go because I didn't have money
The woman said she could put me up if I wanted
negatives: Could you tell me the time?
I could hear what he said.

can_do_statement: Can use 'couldn’t have' + '-ed' to speculate about the past.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses a negative past modal to assert strong improbability or impossibility of a past event.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying something was impossible in the past
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance: stepping back to firmly deduce a negative past conclusion

positives: Surely I couldn't have left it on my seat.
her mother couldn't have hidden it there just like that.
negatives: I couldn't help it.
It could have been worse.

can_do_statement: Can use negative form dare not and daren't +  infinitive without to.

ontology.mental_model: Agent expresses an internal barrier or lack of courage preventing an action using 'dare not' or 'daren't'.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency: grappling with internal fears or boundaries

positives: But many local people dare not go to Lily, because it is too expensive.
they daren't give up their car.
negatives: I dare say you are right.
I didn't dare to move.

can_do_statement: Can use affirmative form dare + infinitive without to.

ontology.mental_model: Agent asserts courage or challenges boundaries by acting, using 'dare' + bare infinitive.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency: asserting volition and overcoming fear

positives: I can cook if you dare eat it!
I wonder if he dare jump.
negatives: How dare you speak to me like that!
I dare not speak.
I dare say you are right.

can_do_statement: Can use semi-modal 'dare' to talk about being brave enough to do something.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses 'dare' as a semi-modal to discuss the internal threshold of courage required for an action.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency: evaluating the fortitude to cross a boundary

positives: I think that they are rather jealous because they daren't give up their car.
She dare not tell him the truth.
negatives: I dare say it will rain.
I double dare you to do it.

can_do_statement: Can use the fixed expression 'I dare say' to say that something is probably true.

ontology.mental_model: Agent uses the fixed phrase 'I dare say' to cautiously assert probability or likely truth.
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance: softening a claim through an epistemic framing device

positives: I dare say that the last option may be the best one.
which I dare say needs improvement.
negatives: I dare you to say that to his face.
I didn't dare to speak.
